title: fix(service-settings): settings audit writes old_hash and the declared SHA-256 digest
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XFdELkVjeF5csUMkbrNabaW)_

Fixes #26465

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:设置审计表 `sys_setting_audit` / `sys_platform_setting_audit` 的 `old_hash` 现在记录写入前那个值的摘要;非密钥值的摘要从 FNV-32 改为列声明的 SHA-256(`sha256:` 前缀)。
- **为什么改**:列声明「旧值的 SHA-256,未设置时为空」,实际 `old_hash` 永远为空、新值是 FNV-32,运维无法从审计轨迹判断一次写入是否真的改了值(重复写入检测失效)。
- **风险与回滚**:不新增任何数据库读取(旧值取自 upsert 已有的存在性探测);密钥值的带密钥摘要路径不变;历史 `fnv32:` 行不回填。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts`(`upsertRow` 返回旧行、`previousAuditDigest`),`src/crypto-adapter.ts`(`settingAuditDigest`),`src/settings-audit-old-hash.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings exec vitest run src/settings-audit-old-hash.test.ts`,预期 7 个用例全绿。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **`old_hash` is written.** `upsertRow` already probes the row at its identity before it updates; it now returns that previous row (snapshotted before the update) beside the `previousEnc` handle it already returned. `setMany` passes `oldHash: previousAuditDigest(previous)` instead of a hard-coded `null`. The read happens under the same identity the write targets: the global rung's `(namespace, key)` in `sys_platform_setting`, and `(organization_id, namespace, key, scope, user_id)` in `sys_setting`. A write with no previous row costs no extra round-trip, because the probe was already there. `old_hash` is null when there was no row, when the row was reset (`value` null), and when the previous row held a secret.
- **The non-secret digest is the declared SHA-256.** A new `settingAuditDigest(canonicalJson)` in `crypto-adapter.ts` returns `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (`stableStringify`, unchanged). The write path uses it for both the new and the previous value instead of `this.crypto.digest(...)`, so an injected `CryptoAdapter` cannot change the column's format. The same `digest` variable feeds the `config_change` row in `sys_audit_log`, so both ledgers keep recording one fingerprint per write.
- **Secret path untouched.** `secretAuditDigest` (the provider's keyed `hmac-sha256:` digest, or null) and its two call sites are byte-identical; a secret write keeps `oldHash: null`.
- **`CryptoAdapter.digest`**: the only non-test caller in the repository was `settings-service.ts:2428`. The interface member stays, so existing adapters still satisfy it. Its docblock and the `NoopCryptoAdapter` FNV comment now say the settings audit no longer reads it.
- **Claim amendment, granted by the seat:** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`, item `platform-core.settings-audit-secret-fingerprint`, revision 4 → 5. Its step-7 positive control computed `fnv32:` for the non-secret `mail.from_email`. After this change that control could never match, and it could no longer prove the offline search works. The control and acceptance[4] now compute `sha256:`. The secret search keeps FNV-1a 32 as a second net, so the item is not loosened. The `history` row says the same.
- **In-package docblock (same claim):** `sys-secret-orphan-report.ts` said the service passes the adapter's `digest()` for non-secret keys. It now names `settingAuditDigest()`.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-settings` patch. `packages/platform-objects` is not touched; the declared columns stand.

## Tests

New `src/settings-audit-old-hash.test.ts` drives `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` through `registerSettingsRoutes` over a real `ObjectQL` with the real `SysSetting` / `SysPlatformSetting` / `SysSecret` / `SysSettingAudit` / `SysPlatformSettingAudit` objects and the plugin's own `buildSettingAuditWriter`. It reads the audit rows back out of the driver store, and computes the expected digests with `node:crypto`, not the implementation:

- tenant rung (`sys_setting_audit`): first set (old null, new `sha256:`), overwrite (old = digest of previous, chained to the prior row's `new_hash`), same-value write (old == new), set → reset → set (reset: old = previous digest, new null; the next set: old null). A null value is the family's removal; the settings routes have no DELETE verb, so reset is the delete case.
- scope: a user-scope write reads its own previous row, not another user's.
- global rung (`sys_platform_setting_audit`): first set, overwrite, same-value write.
- CONTROL, secret value: keyed `hmac-sha256:` `new_hash`, null `old_hash` on both writes, no unkeyed SHA-256 of the secret anywhere in the row.

Updated: `settings-audit-secret-digest.test.ts`, non-secret case: it pinned the adapter's FNV digest; it now pins the `sha256:` digest on both ledgers and that it is not the adapter's.

Ablation, once, on the old-value read: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `oldHash: isEncrypted ? null : SettingsService.previousAuditDigest(previous),` with `oldHash: null,`. The tool's own check confirmed it landed (anchor 1 → 0, blob `7425ed93` → `3b7fd19c`). Result: **5 of 7 red** (overwrite, same-value, set→reset→set, user scope, global rung). The two green are the first-set case and the secret control, which do not depend on the read. Restore was verified: blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test imports `./settings-service.js` from `src/` (no dist hop), so no rebuild was needed between the legs.

Package run on the final head `a397e85a77` (after merging `origin/main` `b7f2b0c290`), under the verify lock: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings build && … typecheck && … exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` → `Test Files 61 passed (61)`, `Tests 1007 passed (1007)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `tsc --listFiles` includes both edited test files. `eslint --no-inline-config packages/services/service-settings/src` exits 0. `test:repo` and dogfood are left to CI: the title has no `!` and there is no `(narrowing)` arm.

## Acceptance notes

- **Mixed history.** Rows written before this change carry `fnv32:` (non-secret) and `hmac-sha256:` (secret). New non-secret rows carry `sha256:`. No reader in the repository compares hashes across rows: `git grep` for `old_hash` / `new_hash` / `newHash` outside service-settings finds only fixtures, docs and the platform-object declarations. A reader that does compare them must compare only same-prefix values. A `fnv32:` row next to a `sha256:` row of the same value reads as "different algorithm", not "different value", because the prefix says so. The first write after upgrading over an `fnv32:` row records `old_hash` as the `sha256:` digest of the stored previous value. It is computed from the value, not copied from the old row, so it does not equal that row's `new_hash` string. Stored rows are not rewritten (ruling).
- **Column docblock vs prefix.** `sys-setting-audit.object.ts:137-142` says "Format: hex SHA-256 of the canonicalised JSON". The stored form is `sha256:` + that hex (71 chars, under `maxLength: 128`). The prefix follows the convention already in the column: `hmac-sha256:` for secrets, `fnv32:` before. The `description` strings ("SHA-256 of the previous value (canonicalised)") hold as written. The TSDoc line does not mention the prefix. It is left as is, because platform-objects is outside the claim.
- **Secret rows keep `old_hash` null.** Writing the previous secret's keyed digest would need a `sys_secret` read plus a decrypt of the previous value on every secret write. The ruling keeps the secret path out of scope, so the "null only when previously unset" declaration is still not met for `encrypted: true` rows.
- **`CryptoAdapter.digest` now has zero non-test readers in this repository.** It is a published interface member, so retiring it is a separate API decision and is not done here.
- Open PRs touching `packages/services/service-settings/**`: none of the 18 open non-bot PRs at start (first page of each PR's files).

## Verification

Each one was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all 64 answered `exit 0`. `dispatch-gates --ran`: "64 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED". The changed-lines reading is 484 (+458 / -26), under the 3000 human-merge threshold.

On the first pass, before the merge, two runs were prerequisite refusals. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 on the shallow clone, and after `git fetch --unshallow origin main` it passed. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 because other packages had no `dist/`. Both answered exit 0 in the final-head pass above, after the merge rebuild.

Every family outside the derivation (artifact rosters, wide-population, the type-check lanes) is left to this PR's CI check-runs.
